result.title: SRA: Selective Residual Adaptation for LLM Reasoning Enhancement
result.summary: Knowledge distillation transfers reasoning capabilities from large language models to lightweight students. However, distilled small models still struggle with multi-step reasoning. We observe that the distribution divergences between teacher and student models along reasoning paths are highly sparse, and target tokens almost always fall within the student top-$K$ candidate set. Based on this finding, unlike approaches updating student backbones or requiring runtime teacher computation, we propose Selective Residual Adaptation (SRA), a plug-and-play framework that internalizes localized corrections. Concretely, SRA employs a Discrepancy Gate to identify divergence positions alongside a Candidate Residual Adapter for top-$K$ logit calibration to correct the mismatch. Theoretically, we establish error bounds ensuring strict sequence level performance gains. Across mathematical benchmarks on Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 4B, SRA consistently enhances distilled student models, raising average Pass@16 by up to 4.37 percentage points while preserving general capabilities.

AI.brief_summary: 论文发现蒸馏学生相对教师的推理路径分歧高度稀疏，且目标 token 几乎总在学生的 top-K 候选内；据此提出 SRA，用 Discrepancy Gate 定位分歧位置、以 Candidate Residual Adapter 做 top-K logit 校准，并给出序列级误差界，在 Qwen3 0.6B–4B 数学基准上提升 Pass@16。
AI.relevance_reason: 「稀疏分歧位置检测 + 局部残差校正」的干预范式可能为 VLM 推理中在关键步骤修正 latent 状态或视觉证据使用提供线索，但该方法只作用于文本 logit，是否涉及内部表示与多步状态更新仍需核查。
